meta.name: golden_aeolus_v1
meta.note: Full accepted run of 2026-08-28: functions -> FCIM -> FHA over all conditions. SF-001-M severity was set by the engineer (was abstained); excluded from abstention metrics via engineerClassified.

functions.subDef: Four podded turbofans produce thrust across the flight envelope. Inputs: fuel at pump inlet pressure (FUE), throttle commands (flight deck via AVI). Outputs: thrust; mechanical drive to generators/EDPs; engine parameter data (AVI). Independence: single-engine failure at/after V1 does not alone cause loss of the top function — continuation to a suitable aerodrome is designed for.
functions.funcDef: Produce and modulate propulsive thrust for all phases of flight, including the engine-out and asymmetric-thrust cases.

functions.subDef: Two inboard reversers provide ground deceleration thrust, inhibited in flight by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement. Inputs: reverse commands (flight deck), WOW/RA (LDG/AVI). Outputs: reverse thrust. Independence: reverser loss does not by itself cause loss of forward thrust.
functions.funcDef: Produce and modulate propulsive thrust for all phases of flight, including the engine-out and asymmetric-thrust cases.

functions.subDef: Position ailerons/spoilers (roll), stabiliser/elevators (pitch) and split rudder (yaw). Inputs: pilot inceptor position, autopilot commands, air/inertial data (AVI). Outputs: surface position and status (AVI). Independence: dual actuation per surface on different hydraulic systems and a mechanical reversion path mean no single supply loss alone defeats control.
functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft about all three axes across the flight envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases.

functions.subDef: Extend/retract Fowler flaps and full-span slats for take-off and landing. Inputs: crew selection, position feedback. Outputs: high-lift position to performance computation (AVI). Independence: two independent PDUs with asymmetry brakes; common torque shaft is a recorded commonality.
functions.funcDef: Position primary and secondary aerodynamic surfaces to control the aircraft about all three axes across the flight envelope, including engine-out and blade-loaded cases.

functions.subDef: Carbon multi-disc braking, normal from HYD B, alternate from HYD A, with accumulator emergency reserve and per-wheel-pair anti-skid. Inputs: pedal/autobrake commands, wheel speed. Outputs: braking; brake temperature (AVI). Independence: dual hydraulic supply plus accumulator sized for six applications; landing margin (1,080 m vs 1,800 m) is the assessment basis.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, absorb ground loads, and provide braking and directional control on the ground.
functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground

functions.subDef: Nose-wheel steering plus main-gear support/flotation spread footprint pressure to the semi-prepared surface. Inputs: tiller/pedal commands. Outputs: gear position (flight deck). Independence: free-fall extension is independent of hydraulic pressure; dual downlock sensing per unit.
functions.funcDef: Support the aircraft on prepared and semi-prepared surfaces, absorb ground loads, and provide braking and directional control on the ground.
functions.funcName: Decelerate and control on the ground

functions.subDef: Twelve rotary latches and eight locking pins on separate supplies secure the visor; a pressure interlock and dual dissimilar sensing confirm the closed/locked state. Inputs: pressurisation state (ECS), crew/ground command. Outputs: lock status (flight deck, take-off config monitor). Independence: two dissimilar independently routed sensing paths; interlock in series with the unlock command. NOTE: the door structural load path itself is STRUCTURE, excluded from functional decomposition.
functions.funcDef: Provide straight-in loading access for a single blade and form part of the pressure boundary and forward structural load path when closed.
functions.funcName: Provide hold access and pressure boundary at the nose

functions.subDef: Nine saddles with two tension straps each provide longitudinal restraint; saddle geometry provides lateral/vertical restraint. Inputs: loading plan, WOW, nose-door position. Outputs: strap tension/saddle engagement (flight deck), mass/distribution to CG computation. Independence: loss of any one strap is carried by neighbours; hold-floor hard points are STRUCTURE with no redundancy (excluded from functional decomposition).
functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t along the full hold length and maintain that restraint through all flight and ground load cases.

functions.subDef: A single instrumented tension loop monitors every strap continuously; loss of tension is annunciated in flight, loss on two adjacent stations as a restraint condition. Inputs: strap tension. Outputs: restraint status (flight deck, take-off config monitor). Independence: single instrumented loop — coverage is a recorded item, not redundant.
functions.funcDef: Receive, position and restrain a single blade of up to 72.6 t along the full hold length and maintain that restraint through all flight and ground load cases.

functions.subDef: Two digital controllers drive two outflow valves (either sufficient), with a pneumatic backup and independent mechanical relief. Inputs: cabin pressure, crew selection, WOW, door position. Outputs: differential/cabin altitude (AVI, crew oxygen logic), pressure state to nose-door interlock. Independence: independent positive/negative relief valves protect structure regardless of the control system.
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control the pressure differential across the fuselage.
functions.funcName: Condition and pressurise the occupied and cargo volumes

functions.subDef: Two air-cycle packs, fed from four engine bleeds through a cross-bleed manifold, condition the flight deck and hold as separate zones. Inputs: bleed air (PRP), ram air, flight-deck selections. Outputs: conditioned air; bleed status to IPS. Independence: either pack from either side; single-pack operation permitted with a reduced hold schedule.
functions.funcDef: Condition and distribute air to the flight deck and hold and control the pressure differential across the fuselage.
functions.funcName: Condition and pressurise the occupied and cargo volumes

functions.subDef: Bleed-air protection of wing leading edges and engine cowls (piccolo); six electrically heated stabiliser zones. Inputs: bleed air, electrical power, TAT/airspeed, crew selection. Outputs: zone health (AVI), bleed demand to ECS. Independence: bleed protection available from either side; electrical zones independently supplied.
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion is unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope.

functions.subDef: Electrically heat probes, static ports, windshields; two ice detectors provide advisory detection with automatic or manual activation. Inputs: electrical power, crew selection. Outputs: ice detection advisory (flight deck). Independence: two detectors — identical in type, commonality is a recorded item.
functions.funcDef: Prevent or remove ice accretion on surfaces, inlets and probes where accretion is unacceptable, for flight in the icing envelope.

functions.subDef: Three display processors drive four displays and two HUDs on dual deterministic networks; three ADIRUs supply air/inertial data; an independent standby instrument shares no supply/sensor/processing. Inputs: system data, sensing, navigation signals, power. Outputs: displays, autopilot/autothrottle commands, recorded parameters. Independence: standby instrument on DC essential shares nothing with the primary displays.
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting for failures and procedures.
functions.subName: Present flight, navigation and system information

functions.subDef: The alerting system consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised alert list with associated procedures. Inputs: status from every system. Outputs: prioritised alerts and procedures to the crew. Independence: two independent processing channels.
functions.funcDef: Acquire, process and present the information the crew needs to fly, navigate and manage the aircraft, and host the alerting for failures and procedures.

functions.subDef: Dual-loop continuous detection per engine nacelle and APU (AND logic degrading to single loop); overheat detection on bleed ducts and gear bays; nine-station hold smoke detection. Inputs: DC essential power, WOW, APU state. Outputs: fire/overheat warnings (AVI). Independence: two loops routed on opposite sides per zone.
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them.

functions.subDef: Two cross-plumbed bottles per engine pair discharged by fire handle; a dedicated APU bottle discharged automatically when unattended. Inputs: hot-battery-bus power, crew commands. Outputs: discharge status, automatic APU shutdown/fuel isolation. Independence: cross-plumbing lets either bottle serve either nacelle of the pair. NOTE: hold has detection but no suppression — a recorded decision to substantiate.
functions.funcDef: Detect fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected and provide the means to extinguish or suppress them.

functions.subDef: Two high-pressure cylinders feed a common manifold with a crossover valve to four quick-donning masks with demand regulators, sized for four occupants for the diversion time with reserve. Inputs: crew donning action, cabin altitude signal (ECS). Outputs: oxygen to four stations; cylinder pressure/status (flight deck). Independence: either cylinder supplies the crew for the required duration at reduced reserve; regulators independent per mask.
functions.funcDef: Supply breathing oxygen to the flight crew for loss of pressurisation, smoke and fume events, and the ensuing descent and diversion.

fha.effAc: Aircraft thrust does not match commanded value; magnitude and direction (over/under, symmetric/asymmetric) not bounded by the SDD. An erroneous high or asymmetric response at low speed could produce a trajectory or directional-control demand up to the outboard-engine sizing case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous thrust response to crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew detect via thrust/engine parameter displays and airspeed; assumed to revert to manual thrust and manage asymmetry with rudder within the sized directional authority.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not bound the MAGNITUDE, symmetry or controllability of an erroneous thrust response, so the worst-case aircraft effect (from a nuisance offset up to an uncontrollable asymmetric excursion at low speed) cannot be established from the function definition alone. Need the erroneous-response envelope (max deviation, single vs multi-engine, phase) to derive severity.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Thrust changes on one or more engines with no crew command; if asymmetric, imposes a directional-control demand up to the outboard-engine case (28 m moment arm, 0.35 semi-span) which is the sizing case for rudder authority. Magnitude and number of affected engines not bounded by the SDD.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded thrust change with no command
fha.effCrew: Crew detect via engine/thrust displays and aircraft response; assumed to counter with rudder within sized authority and isolate the affected engine via fuel shut-off/fire handle.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD establishes the outboard-engine asymmetry as the directional sizing case but does not bound the magnitude of an UNCOMMANDED excursion or whether it can affect more than one engine, so worst-case effect and residual controllability cannot be derived from the function definition. Need the uncommanded-change envelope.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: A slow thrust drift accumulates below the detection threshold; if asymmetric it produces a slowly increasing directional/trim demand that is not annunciated. Because it is sub-threshold the crew take no corrective action, so the drift can develop toward the outboard-engine asymmetry case before it becomes apparent.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded thrust drift developing below detection threshold (crew unaware)
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware by definition; assumed to continue normal duties and take no action regarding the drift until it exceeds detection/annunciation, at which point they revert to the aware case.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD does not state the detection threshold, the drift rate, or the maximum asymmetry that can accumulate undetected, so the worst-case effect of the unaware condition (which routinely drives severity higher than the aware case) cannot be derived. Need the sub-threshold drift envelope and monitoring coverage.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced total thrust with residual asymmetry inside the controllable limits sized by the flight controls; aircraft designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome following loss of any one engine at or after V1. Performance (climb, obstacle, range) degraded but flight path maintainable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust with asymmetry within controllable limits
fha.effCrew: Crew detect via engine parameters and asymmetry cues; assumed to apply rudder within sized authority, secure the affected engine (fuel shut-off/fire handle) and continue to a suitable aerodrome per the one-engine-out dispatch case.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Proposed direction is toward the lower end because the SDD states the aircraft is designed to continue to a suitable aerodrome after loss of any one engine at/after V1 and this condition is bounded to WITHIN controllable limits; however severity left empty because the SDD does not state the resulting performance margin at max blade payload (climb gradient, obstacle clearance, range effect) needed to confirm the class. Confirm against one-engine-inop performance data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Loss of thrust producing one-sided asymmetry beyond the single-engine dispatch case. The SDD identifies loss of a second engine on the same side as OUTSIDE the design dispatch case and retained as a condition to be studied; the directional-control demand may exceed the sized single-supply rudder authority, threatening trajectory control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of thrust — asymmetry from one side (loss of a second engine on the same side)
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum rudder within available authority; the SDD does not establish that residual authority is sufficient for a two-engine same-side loss, so successful control is not assured.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD explicitly holds a second same-side engine loss as OUTSIDE the design dispatch case and 'a condition to be studied', so the aircraft effect (controllable vs loss of control) is not established. Severity left empty pending the directional-control study for the two-engine same-side case at max blade payload.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Aircraft loses all propulsive thrust from the four podded turbofans; no means to generate or control thrust remains. Aircraft becomes a glider with a forced descent; a controlled forced landing on a suitable surface is not assured in most phases.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried. Flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of propulsive thrust (all four engines)
fha.effCrew: Crew must manage an unpowered descent and attempt a forced landing; high workload with no thrust available for go-around or terrain avoidance.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of thrust across all four engines removes the ability to sustain flight; a survivable outcome is not assured across the flight envelope. Effects support Catastrophic per AC 25.1309-1B (objective Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh). PROPOSED for engineer confirmation. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Uncommanded reverse thrust on an inboard engine. In flight, an uncommanded deployment produces asymmetric drag/thrust and a yawing/rolling upset; on the ground it produces unexpected deceleration and asymmetry. Reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only, and in-flight deployment is inhibited by weight-on-wheels and radio-altimeter agreement with a mechanical sleeve lock.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Reverse thrust provided when not commanded
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the uncommanded deployment and counter the resulting asymmetry; workload and controllability depend on phase and on whether an in-flight inhibit has been defeated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Severity depends on whether the condition can occur in flight (all three inhibits — WOW, radio-altimeter agreement, mechanical sleeve lock — defeated) versus on the ground, and on the resulting controllability at the outboard/inboard moment arms. The SDD gives the inhibit architecture but not the controllability outcome of an in-flight inboard-reverser deployment; without that effect on aircraft trajectory the aircraft-level severity cannot be derived. Left blank pending flight-control/controllability data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reverse deployed on one inboard engine but not the other, producing a yawing moment during landing rollout on a semi-prepared surface. Directional control must be held by steering/rudder while decelerating within the available strip.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Reverse thrust asymmetry between sides during ground rollout
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the asymmetry and counter the yaw with steering and differential braking during rollout; workload elevated on the semi-prepared strip.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The SDD gives reverser fitment to the two inboard engines and the 1,800 m requirement against ~1,080 m predicted rollout, but does not quantify the directional-control consequence or stopping-distance shortfall of a single-side reverse asymmetry on the semi-prepared surface. Aircraft effect (departure/overrun outcome) is not derivable from the provided data, so severity is left blank. NOTE: this condition has no FCIM cell for SF-002 yet.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Ground reverse thrust unavailable at touchdown, unknown to the crew, so deceleration relies on wheel braking alone. On the semi-prepared strip the stopping performance falls back on the braking design and the margin between the 1,800 m requirement and the ~1,080 m predicted rollout.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Undetected loss of reverse availability before landing rollout
fha.effCrew: Crew expect reverse and do not obtain it at touchdown; must decelerate on braking alone with no prior configuration for the shortfall.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Whether loss of reverse alone causes an overrun depends on the braking-only stopping distance on the semi-prepared surface versus 1,800 m — the SDD states the landing requirement and predicted rollout but does not state the braking-only case with reverse credited or not. Without the overrun outcome the aircraft effect cannot be classified; severity left blank pending performance data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced reverse deceleration during landing rollout; increased reliance on wheel braking to stop within the available strip on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of ground reverse effectiveness
fha.effCrew: Crew apply additional braking to compensate for reduced reverse; deceleration achievable within the available margin depending on the shortfall.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The magnitude of the deceleration shortfall and its effect on stopping distance versus the 1,800 m requirement is not quantified in the SDD, so no aircraft-level effect (overrun risk) can be derived. Severity left blank pending landing-performance data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: On landing rollout the aircraft is decelerated by wheel braking alone with no reverse-thrust contribution; stopping distance increases. On the semi-prepared destination strip the 1,800 m landing requirement against a predicted ~1,080 m rollout provides margin, but that margin is eroded and any additional degradation (wet/contaminated surface, brake degradation) reduces it further.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground thrust reversing
fha.effCrew: Crew commands reverse and it is unavailable/annunciated; crew rely on wheel braking and remaining stopping means, increasing workload and requiring earlier/harder braking.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Reversers are fitted to the two inboard engines only and are a supplementary decelerating means; wheel braking (accumulator-supported, sized to six applications with all three hydraulic systems lost) remains the primary stopping means, and the 1,080 m predicted rollout sits inside the 1,800 m requirement. Effect is a significant reduction in stopping margin on a semi-prepared surface with increased crew workload — proposed Major. Confirm against overrun analysis on the semi-prepared surface with concurrent braking degradation; if margin can be exhausted under credible concurrent conditions this may rise to Hazardous. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Pitch axis responds differently from the commanded input, producing an unintended flight-path/attitude change in pitch; if the error is large or occurs at low altitude the aircraft departs its intended trajectory with limited time and height for recovery.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous pitch response to crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives aircraft not following pitch command; must detect, diagnose and counter an erroneous response, potentially against envelope-protection or degraded-law behaviour, under high workload and short timescales near the ground.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Primary flight-path control is a flight-critical function; an erroneous pitch response drives the aircraft off its commanded trajectory and, at low altitude/high speed, credibly prevents continued safe flight and landing — proposed Catastrophic. Confirm the worst-case magnitude and phase, and whether the fly-by-wire architecture (three dissimilar FCCs, envelope protection, mechanical stabiliser-trim reversion) bounds the erroneous authority to a less-severe class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Aircraft develops a pitch motion / flight-path change in the absence of any crew command; an uncommanded pitch excursion changes attitude and trajectory and, if rapid or at low altitude, exceeds the time/height available to arrest it.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded pitch motion with no command
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise an uncommanded departure they did not initiate, override or counter it, and manage any degraded control law — a demanding recognition-and-recovery task, most severe at low altitude.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded pitch excursion on the primary flight-path axis can drive the aircraft off its trajectory with no crew initiation and, at low altitude/high speed, credibly precludes continued safe flight and landing — proposed Catastrophic. Confirm the worst-case rate/magnitude and phase, and whether the architecture bounds the uncommanded authority. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Roll axis responds differently from the commanded input, producing an unintended bank/flight-path change in roll; a large or low-altitude error causes departure from the intended lateral trajectory, and roll asymmetry compounds directional control in the engine-out / maximum-blade sizing case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous roll response to crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives the aircraft not following the roll command; must detect and counter an erroneous lateral response, potentially with degraded control law, under high workload near the ground.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Erroneous roll on the primary flight-path axis drives the aircraft off its commanded lateral trajectory; at low altitude/high speed this credibly precludes continued safe flight and landing — proposed Catastrophic. Confirm worst-case magnitude/phase and whether the dual-actuation/dissimilar-FCC architecture bounds the erroneous roll authority. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Aircraft develops an uncommanded roll/bank in the absence of any crew command; the lateral excursion changes trajectory and, if rapid or at low altitude, exceeds the time/height available to arrest it, with directional coupling in the engine-out / maximum-blade case.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded roll motion with no command
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise an uncommanded lateral departure they did not initiate and counter it, managing any degraded law — a demanding recognition-and-recovery task, most severe at low altitude.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: An uncommanded roll excursion on the primary flight-path axis can drive the aircraft off its lateral trajectory with no crew initiation and, at low altitude/high speed, credibly precludes continued safe flight and landing — proposed Catastrophic. Confirm worst-case rate/magnitude/phase and whether the architecture bounds the uncommanded roll authority. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Aircraft yaws in a direction or to an extent other than commanded; superimposed on the directional-control sizing case (outboard engine-out at 28 m moment arm) an erroneous yaw response reduces the available authority margin and can produce sideslip/heading excursions and, in the take-off/landing regime, lateral path deviation.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous yaw response to crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise the erroneous response and counter through split-rudder segments and degraded control laws; increased workload and reduced margin during critical phases.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Hazardous (↔ Extremely Remote, 1e-7/fh): erroneous yaw degrades directional control which the SDD identifies as the sizing case (outboard engine-out, 28 m arm), plausibly severe but recoverable via split-rudder segments/degraded laws — not shown Catastrophic. Confirm against a substantiated controllability effect; the aircraft-level excursion magnitude is design-informed, not established. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Aircraft develops yaw/sideslip with no crew command; heading and flight-path excursion that, near the ground on a semi-prepared strip, threatens lateral path control and, at altitude, imposes sideslip against the directional-control margin sized for engine-out.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded yaw motion with no command
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect the uncommanded motion and arrest it through rudder/roll inputs and available control laws; workload and startle in critical phases.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Hazardous (↔ Extremely Remote, 1e-7/fh): an uncommanded yaw is annunciated/perceptible (aware) and countered through the split-rudder architecture, credibly severe but recoverable — not shown Catastrophic. Confirm against a substantiated controllability/excursion effect before fixing the class. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded pitch divergence accumulates below the detection threshold; with the crew unaware and taking no corrective action, the aircraft drifts toward an out-of-trim/attitude excursion, potentially reaching an unrecoverable pitch state or airspeed/attitude departure before it is recognised.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded pitch motion developing below detection threshold
fha.effCrew: By construction the crew are unaware and continue normal duties, taking no action; recognition occurs only once the divergence exceeds the threshold, by which point margin may be lost.

Severity rationale: PROPOSED Catastrophic (↔ Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh): the unaware, below-threshold nature removes crew mitigation, so a slow pitch divergence can develop unchecked to a hazardous/unrecoverable attitude. Confirm the assumed no-crew-action and the accumulated-excursion effect; the terminal aircraft state is design-informed, not substantiated by the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: A slow uncommanded roll accumulates below the detection threshold; with the crew unaware and taking no action, bank angle diverges toward a spiral/attitude excursion that may reach an unrecoverable state or path departure before recognition.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Slow uncommanded roll motion developing below detection threshold
fha.effCrew: By construction the crew are unaware and continue normal duties, taking no action; recognition occurs only after the divergence exceeds the threshold.

Confirm the no-crew-action assumption and the accumulated-excursion effect; the terminal state is design-informed, not established. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.

Confirm the no-crew-action assumption and the accumulated-excursion/roll-coupling effect; the terminal state is design-informed, not substantiated. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Reduced pitch control authority; flight-path control retained but with reduced margin, particularly in the blade-loaded and manoeuvring cases. Redundant actuation (elevators on HYD A and C) means partial loss leaves a means of pitch control.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of pitch control authority (control of primary flight-path axes degraded in pitch; still controllable at reduced authority)
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Increased crew workload to maintain flight path; degraded-law annunciation; may require configuration/speed management.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single classification: outcome spans Major (workload/margin reduction with control retained) up to Hazardous depending on how much pitch authority is lost and in which phase (approach/landing at blade payload). The function definition 'Control primary flight-path axes' and the FCIM text 'Partial loss of pitch control authority' do not quantify the residual authority, so the per-phase worst-case effect cannot be established. Needs the residual-authority definition and the sizing case for pitch to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Loss of ability to control the aircraft's trajectory about the primary axes. A mechanical reversion path to stabiliser trim and the lower rudder segment provides a survivable but degraded means of control with all three flight control computers lost; complete loss of primary flight-path control by all means is a loss of continued safe flight and landing.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of primary flight-path control (aircraft trajectory cannot be controlled by any primary means)
fha.phases: Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Inability to control the flight path; crew action confined to any surviving reversion means.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Complete loss of primary flight-path control prevents continued safe flight and landing, an effect classified Catastrophic; per §25.1309/AC 25.1309-1B the paired safety objective is Extremely Improbable (target 1e-9/fh). Proposed for engineer confirmation. The SDD mechanical reversion path is a mitigation whose adequacy is an SFHA/architecture question, not a reason to down-classify the aircraft-level total-loss condition. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces at a position inconsistent with the commanded configuration. Symmetric mis-position degrades the low-speed lift/performance schedule at takeoff and landing; an asymmetric position (flaps/slats) produces a rolling moment. The high-lift drive is two PDUs through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section, which bound but do not preclude a mismatch. Effect is most significant in the low-speed takeoff and landing phases where high-lift is required.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous high-lift position versus commanded (high-lift surfaces at a position different from that commanded, including asymmetric position)
fha.effCrew: Configuration warning/annunciation; crew workload to manage the mis-configuration and to control any resulting asymmetry; possible performance re-assessment.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a single classification: a symmetric mis-position affecting the takeoff/landing performance schedule and a large asymmetric deployment producing an uncontrolled rolling moment sit at different points on the ladder (roughly Major to Hazardous), and the FCIM text 'Erroneous high-lift position versus commanded' does not distinguish symmetric from asymmetric or state the magnitude. The per-phase worst-case effect cannot be established without the mis-position magnitude/asymmetry envelope; classify once that is defined.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: High-lift surfaces (flaps/slats) move without crew command, producing an unexpected change in configuration: lift, drag and pitching-moment change abruptly. Uncommanded extension at high speed risks structural overload of the surfaces and unexpected trim change; uncommanded retraction at low speed reduces stall margin. Effect worst on approach/landing and at high-speed cruise.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded high-lift movement with no command
fha.effCrew: Crew face an unexpected, unannounced configuration change requiring immediate recognition and manual intervention (trim, speed, possible law reversion); increased workload during a critical phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a defensible single classification from the function definition alone: outcome spans loss of stall margin (low speed) to structural overspeed of the surface (high speed), and the SDD's asymmetry brakes and PDU architecture do not state the achievable rate, symmetry or envelope of an uncommanded movement. Effect could be Hazardous or Catastrophic depending on speed at onset and whether motion is symmetric — left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced high-lift authority available symmetrically; achievable lift coefficient at low speed is degraded, raising required approach and take-off speeds and lengthening take-off and landing distance. On a semi-prepared 1,800 m strip against a ~1,080 m predicted rollout, the margin for landing is eroded. Aircraft remains controllable; performance is reduced.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Symmetric partial loss of high-lift
fha.effCrew: Crew fly a higher-speed, longer-field approach/departure using degraded-configuration procedures and revised performance; increased workload and reduced margin but a flyable configuration.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Symmetric partial loss degrades low-speed performance and field margin without loss of control; a significant reduction in safety margin / functional capability and increased crew workload consistent with Major. PROPOSED — confirm against the actual achievable degraded-flap performance and the semi-prepared-strip landing margin. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Left/right high-lift surfaces reach different positions, producing a rolling moment and lift asymmetry at low speed. Asymmetry brakes at each section are provided to arrest a runaway on one side; with that protection the residual asymmetry produces a roll/yaw disturbance the flight controls must trim out. Uncontrolled asymmetry near stall speed could exceed lateral control authority.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric high-lift deployment between sides
fha.effCrew: Crew must recognise and counter an unexpected roll/yaw at low speed, apply lateral control and follow asymmetry procedure; high workload at a critical, low-margin phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Classification depends on the maximum asymmetry the asymmetry brakes permit before arrest and whether residual roll is within lateral control authority at approach speed — the SDD confirms asymmetry brakes exist but does not quantify the tripped asymmetry or the resulting roll. With protection failed the condition could reach Hazardous/Catastrophic; with protection working it may be Major. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No high-lift available: flaps and slats unavailable, so the aircraft must take off and land in the clean configuration at substantially higher speeds. Take-off and landing distances increase markedly; on a 1,800 m semi-prepared strip against a ~1,080 m predicted (flapped) rollout the required landing distance may exceed the available field. Aircraft remains controllable but low-speed performance and field capability are severely degraded.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of high-lift capability
fha.effCrew: Crew execute a flapless/slatless take-off or landing at higher speed with degraded field performance, possibly requiring diversion to a longer surface; significant increase in workload and required procedure.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect hinges on whether a flapless landing remains within the 1,800 m semi-prepared field limit and whether a suitable alternate exists; the SDD gives the field requirement and flapped rollout but not the clean-configuration landing distance, so I cannot ground whether the outcome is a large margin reduction (Major/Hazardous) or an unachievable landing (approaching Catastrophic). Left empty pending clean-configuration performance data.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Wheel braking applies without crew command. During the take-off roll this produces unexpected deceleration and, if asymmetric across bogies, a yaw/directional excursion on a semi-prepared strip; may compromise take-off performance or cause a directional departure. During taxi, uncommanded braking causes a stop or heading deviation. Anti-skid is per wheel pair; carbon multi-disc brakes could overheat under sustained uncommanded application.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded brake application with no command
fha.effCrew: Crew must detect unexpected deceleration or heading change, override or isolate braking and maintain directional control; high workload during the take-off roll where speed and field margin are critical.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Directional and deceleration effect during the take-off roll on a semi-prepared surface with a 72.6 t single blade could range from a rejected-take-off performance loss (Major) to a directional departure off a 1,800 m strip (Hazardous), depending on the number of bogies affected, symmetry and onset speed — none of which the function definition or SDD quantify. Left empty pending that determination.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Deceleration differs from that commanded; may under- or over-brake relative to pilot demand, degrading achieved stopping performance against the 1,800 m semi-prepared landing distance requirement (predicted rollout ~1,080 m).
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous braking response to crew command (braking magnitude or timing differs from commanded, excluding uncommanded application and total loss)
fha.effCrew: Crew perceives aircraft not decelerating as commanded and must react with alternate braking/reverse; increased workload and reduced margin on a short semi-prepared surface.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect direction is grounded but magnitude is not: the function definition does not state HOW MUCH the braking error is, whether it consistently over- or under-brakes, or whether the 1,800 m/1,080 m margin is exceeded. Severity spans Major to Hazardous depending on error magnitude and runway margin consumed — cannot derive a single class without that. Engineer to bound the error and confirm against the landing-distance margin.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced deceleration capability; increased stopping distance consuming the margin between predicted rollout (~1,080 m) and the 1,800 m semi-prepared requirement, aided by inboard reversers.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.fcDesc: Partial loss of wheel braking capacity (braking still available but at reduced deceleration capability)
fha.effCrew: Crew becomes aware via degraded deceleration and system indication; applies maximum braking and reverse; manages increased stopping distance.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Magnitude of the capacity loss is not stated by the function definition (loss of one system supply vs several bogies vs one bogie). Outcome ranges from Minor/Major (within remaining margin) to Hazardous (margin exceeded, overrun). Cannot derive a single class without the degree of loss and the resulting stopping distance against the 1,800 m requirement. Engineer to quantify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Without per-wheel-pair anti-skid, braking on a semi-prepared (low, variable friction) surface risks wheel lock, tyre burst and loss of achievable deceleration and directional stability; effective braking distance increases and may exceed the 1,800 m requirement.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of anti-skid function (braking available but wheel-pair skid protection lost)
fha.effCrew: Crew must modulate braking manually to avoid lockup on a low-friction surface; substantially increased workload at the highest-energy phase; degraded directional control if tyres skid asymmetrically.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Grounded that anti-skid is per-wheel-pair and the surface is semi-prepared/low-friction, so loss is significant. But the achievable braking WITHOUT anti-skid on this surface, and whether it stays within the 1,800 m margin, is not stated — outcome could be Major (manageable with increased distance) or Hazardous (overrun on low friction). Left empty pending performance/friction data. Note this id is not in the current FCIM SF-005 cell.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Unequal braking produces a yawing moment during the ground roll, tending to swing the aircraft off the runway centreline; on a narrow semi-prepared strip this threatens directional control and lateral runway departure.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers.
fha.fcDesc: Asymmetric braking between sides (unequal braking effort left versus right)
fha.effCrew: Crew must counter the induced yaw with steering and differential technique while decelerating at high energy; workload elevated; risk of loss of directional control if the asymmetry exceeds correction authority.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect (directional upset from a yaw moment) is grounded, but the MAGNITUDE of the asymmetry and whether nose-wheel steering/rudder authority can counter it on a semi-prepared surface is not stated by the function definition. Outcome ranges Major (correctable) to Hazardous (loss of directional control / lateral departure). Left empty pending the controllable-asymmetry limit. Engineer to bound.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No wheel braking available on the ground; deceleration must rely on reverse thrust (inboard engines only), aerodynamic drag and remaining rollout margin. Against an 1,800 m semi-prepared landing requirement with predicted rollout ~1,080 m, complete loss of braking credibly consumes the margin and risks runway/strip overrun, particularly on a rejected take-off at high energy.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only. Occupants exposed to overrun-related deceleration and potential impact.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of wheel braking
fha.effCrew: Crew apply maximum available deceleration (reverse thrust, steering to remain on surface) with markedly increased workload and no braking authority; directional and stopping control significantly degraded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Derived from stated effects: total loss of wheel braking against a narrow strip margin credibly leads to overrun with significant reduction in safety margins and higher crew workload, but multiple compensating means (reverse thrust, accumulator reserve elsewhere, rollout margin) and the discrete high-energy exposure make Catastrophic not clearly supported by the stated effects. PROPOSED — confirm; the RTO high-energy phase may drive worse and warrants engineering review. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Ground directional path departs from crew intent following a steering command; at take-off/landing ground speed an erroneous steering response can produce lateral excursion toward runway/strip edge before the crew corrects, with risk of departure from the prepared surface.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only. Occupants exposed to lateral-excursion/veer effects on the ground.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous ground steering response to crew command
fha.effCrew: Crew detect a steering response inconsistent with command, revert to differential braking/rudder and reduce command authority, with increased workload during a ground-speed-critical phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the magnitude/authority of the erroneous steering response and the speed at which it manifests are not stated in the provided function definition, and outcome ranges from a controllable veer (Major) to a high-speed excursion (potentially Hazardous). Missing: erroneous-command authority limit, phase-speed exposure, and available crew reversion effectiveness. Engineer to supply.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Nose-wheel deflects without command; on the ground at speed an uncommanded deflection induces an unintended turning moment and lateral path departure, risking runway/strip excursion before the crew arrests it.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only. Occupants exposed to excursion/veer effects.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose-wheel steering deflection
fha.effCrew: Crew perceive the veer, counter with rudder/differential braking and, where provided, disconnect/override steering; workload elevated during a critical ground phase.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: deflection magnitude and the ground speed at onset are not stated in the provided function definition, so the aircraft effect ranges from a correctable veer to a high-speed excursion; and the crew's reversion/disconnect effectiveness against an uncommanded deflection is not established. Missing: deflection authority, phase-speed exposure, override effectiveness. Engineer to supply.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: An uncommanded nose-wheel deflection develops below the crew detection threshold, so no timely corrective action is taken; the unintended turning moment accumulates and the ground path diverges, with the crew continuing normal duties (unaware) until the divergence becomes apparent, credibly later than for the aware case.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only. Occupants exposed to delayed-onset excursion effects.
fha.fcDesc: Uncommanded nose-wheel steering deflection developing below crew detection
fha.effCrew: Per the unaware assumption the crew take no action regarding the condition and continue normal duties; correction is delayed until the path divergence is otherwise detected, by which point corrective authority may be reduced.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: the deflection rate/authority and the ground-speed phase at which the unaware divergence culminates are not stated in the provided function definition, so the aircraft effect (delayed excursion) cannot be bounded. The unaware assumption typically worsens the class versus the aware case, but the magnitude is undetermined. Missing: undetected deflection rate/authority, detection threshold, phase-speed exposure. Engineer to supply.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Ground directional steering is available but at reduced authority; crew retain directional control using reduced steering plus differential braking and rudder, with reduced margin to hold the intended path in crosswind or on a semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: No passengers carried; flight crew only.
fha.fcDesc: Reduced ground steering authority
fha.effCrew: Crew compensate with differential braking and rudder for the reduced steering authority; workload increased but directional control retained.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground a severity: 'reduced' does not quantify the residual steering authority left, and the provided function definition does not state whether remaining authority (with differential braking/rudder) preserves directional control on the semi-prepared strip in the sizing crosswind. Outcome ranges from Minor to Major depending on residual authority. Missing: residual authority level and demonstrated adequacy of alternate directional means. Engineer to supply.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Reduced ground steering input path; nose-wheel steering still commandable through rudder pedals, giving degraded but continued directional control on the ground.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; no effect.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of tiller steering with rudder-pedal steering retained
fha.effCrew: Crew reverts to pedal steering; increased workload for tight-radius manoeuvring on a semi-prepared strip.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A degraded-capability partial loss with a retained pedal steering path per SDD ('commanded from tillers and rudder pedals'); confirm the pedal-only authority is adequate for the semi-prepared taxi/turnaround case before accepting Minor. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No steering of the nose wheel; directional control on the ground must be maintained by other means (differential braking/rudder) if available; risk of runway/strip departure on a 1,800 m semi-prepared surface.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; no effect.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of ground directional steering
fha.effCrew: Crew attempts directional control by alternate means; high workload during rollout deceleration.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Effect stated, but the SDD does not quantify residual directional control by differential braking or rudder aerodynamics on the ground, nor the strip lateral margin; cannot derive severity without the directional-control-margin case. Leave EMPTY for engineering judgment.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Crew and take-off configuration monitor believe the door is locked when it is not; the door forms part of the pressure boundary and forward fuselage structural load path, so an unlocked door under flight/pressure loads can open in flight with loss of structural integrity and rapid depressurisation.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; crew exposed to depressurisation and potential structural failure.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous locked indication with nose door actually unlocked
fha.effCrew: Crew unaware; no corrective action taken because indication is false.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Proposed Catastrophic: SDD states the door 'forms part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path when closed'; a falsely-indicated locked door departing in flight is a candidate for loss of the aircraft. Confirm whether the dual dissimilar sensing and take-off config check defeat this single-indication failure before accepting. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Unlock actuation with residual differential present could allow uncontrolled door movement and rapid venting of the pressurised hold; SDD states the interlock should prevent unlock above 0.1 psi and that the door cannot be operated in flight.
fha.effPax: No occupants in hold; no effect.
fha.fcDesc: Unlock command permitted with the hold pressurised
fha.effCrew: Crew/ground on the flight deck; exposure to sudden door release and pressure discharge during a ground operation.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — The door 'cannot be operated in flight' and the interlock confirms differential below 0.1 psi, so the exposed case is a ground unlock with residual differential; the SDD does not state the energy released or personnel exposure, so the aircraft/occupant effect cannot be graded. Leave EMPTY.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Fewer than the eight independent locking pins engaged; twelve rotary latches remain and the pins prevent latch back-drive. Load path and pressure boundary degraded but retained; residual structural and pressure-holding margin depends on how many pins remain and is not quantified in the description.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants affected.
fha.fcDesc: Reduced number of engaged nose-door locking pins with door still locked
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — SDD §5.7.2 establishes 8 pins plus 12 latches but gives no substantiation of the margin at a reduced pin count, and does not state whether a reduced count is annunciated to the crew or how they would act. Aircraft effect (retained vs. failed pressure boundary) cannot be bounded from the description, so severity cannot be derived. Needs structural/pressure-margin substantiation and crew-awareness definition.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: With all latches and pins unlocked, the visor forms part of the pressure boundary and the forward fuselage structural load path (§5.7.1). Loss of locking in flight risks door displacement, loss of the forward load path and rapid depressurisation of the pressure boundary. The pressure interlock prevents unlock while pressurised, so this condition presumes failure of that interlock or an in-flight structural release.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants aboard, but structural/pressure loss threatens the airframe and crew.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of nose-door locking capability
fha.effCrew: Crew alerted via lock-status indication (annunciated at all times per §5.7.6) and take-off configuration monitor; no in-flight means to re-secure the door — door cannot be operated in flight.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: SDD §5.7.1: door is pressure boundary and forward-fuselage structural load path when closed, single load path treated as structure (§5.7.3). In-flight loss of the primary structural load path / pressure boundary is a candidate Catastrophic condition (Extremely Improbable objective, 1e-9/fh). Proposed pending confirmation of the in-flight release scenario and the special-condition treatment of the door as a primary structural/pressure element (§1.3). — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Uncommanded release of restraint on a single 72.6 t blade occupying the full 108 m hold length permits longitudinal shift of a large mass, driving a rapid centre-of-gravity excursion and potential secondary structural/hold damage; lateral and vertical restraint by saddle geometry may not arrest a longitudinal runaway.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants in the hold, but a CG excursion threatens controllability and the airframe.
fha.fcDesc: Payload restraint releasing without command in flight
fha.effCrew: Restraint status and strap tension are indicated to the flight deck; loss annunciated in flight (§5.8.2) but there is no in-flight adjustment of restraint (§5.8.6), so the crew have indication only and no means to re-secure the blade.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: A 72.6 t single unitised mass shifting longitudinally the length of a 108 m hold is a candidate loss-of-control / structural-overload condition with no in-flight recovery means. Proposed Catastrophic (Extremely Improbable, 1e-9/fh) derived from the mass, hold length and absence of in-flight restraint adjustment; pending confirmation of the achievable CG excursion and controllability limits, which the SDD does not quantify. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Longitudinal restraint margin on the 72.6 t blade reduced across multiple stations; blade may creep against saddle geometry under manoeuvre/gust loads, with potential for CG movement toward or beyond limits during flight.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Reduced restraint tension across the payload
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: Reduced tension annunciated via the tension-monitoring loop; crew has indication only and no in-flight adjustment; response limited to manoeuvre limitation / diversion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: the SDD states load paths are sized so loss of any ONE strap is carried by neighbours, but gives no substantiation of the aircraft effect of a general tension reduction across stations (whether it produces a controllable CG creep or an uncontrolled shift). Requires restraint-load / CG-excursion analysis to classify.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Single-station tension lost; load carried by neighbouring straps per the sized load paths, so restraint retained but with reduced margin; undetected, so no crew mitigation and potential progression to an adjacent station.
fha.effPax: N/A — hold unoccupied in flight; no passengers carried.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of restraint tension at a single station developing undetected
fha.phases: Taxi, Takeoff, Climb, Cruise, Descent, Approach, Landing
fha.effCrew: By definition undetected: crew continue duties normally and take no action; no annunciation received.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot ground severity: SDD states loss of any one strap is carried by neighbours (implying benign single-station effect) but also that the tension loop is a single instrumented loop of recorded coverage — the 'undetected' path depends on whether the monitoring gap can allow progression to adjacent stations before a hazardous condition arises. Requires restraint-load and monitoring-coverage analysis.. Engineer to classify.
