fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of flight, navigation and system information including the standby instrument
fha.effCrew: Crew have no valid reference to fly, navigate or manage the aircraft; loss of control likely.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of all flight/nav/system information including the independent standby removes every valid reference; continued safe flight cannot be assured. Proposed Catastrophic — confirm the condition is defined to include loss of the standby (the standby is stated to share nothing with the primaries). — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft state; potential for inappropriate crew response to a false alert, or desensitisation reducing response to genuine alerts.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Erroneous or spurious crew alert presented by the consolidated alerting system with no genuine failure condition present
fha.effCrew: Crew presented with a false or spurious alert on the consolidated prioritised list; nuisance and workload increase, potential distraction or unwarranted procedure execution; two independent alerting channels provide comparison.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — A single spurious alert's aircraft-level consequence depends on which alert and whether it triggers an inappropriate crew action or masks/desensitises genuine alerts — the SDD describes the alerting architecture (single prioritised list, two independent channels) but not the effect of a specific erroneous alert on the aircraft, so the effect and hence severity cannot be grounded. Left amber; do not default to No Safety Effect.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of alert consolidation — system status no longer consolidated into a single prioritised crew alert list
fha.effCrew: Crew lose the single consolidated alert list; system status and associated procedures must be sought from individual system indications, increasing the effort to identify what has failed and what to do about it.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: SDD states AVI 'consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list with associated procedures' but gives no aircraft-level effect or crew-workload consequence of losing that consolidation in worst-case phase. Severity turns on crew detection of underlying failures and workload — a human-factors judgement not in the provided material. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of alert prioritisation — alerts still presented but no longer ordered by priority
fha.effCrew: Alerts remain visible but are not prioritised; crew must themselves establish which alert to act on first, degrading timely response to the most safety-significant condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: SDD describes a 'prioritised' alert list but states no aircraft-level effect of losing prioritisation and no crew-workload consequence. Severity depends on the underlying condition mis-ordered and crew response — not in the provided material. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Undetected suppression of a required alert — an alert that should be presented is silently withheld
fha.effCrew: An alert the crew are entitled to receive is suppressed without indication; crew continue their duties unaware of the underlying condition and take no action regarding it, with the consequence set by the severity of the unannunciated condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: this is an unaware condition whose severity is that of the underlying failure the alert governs. The SDD does not enumerate which conditions the alerting suppresses nor their aircraft effect, so the worst-case underlying severity cannot be derived from the provided material. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Mis-prioritised crew alert list — alerts presented in an erroneous order of priority
fha.effCrew: A lower-priority alert is presented ahead of a higher-priority one; crew may act on the wrong condition first or delay response to the most safety-significant alert, with the consequence set by the mis-ordered condition.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: SDD states the list is 'prioritised' but gives no aircraft-level effect of erroneous prioritisation. Severity depends on which underlying condition is delayed and crew response under workload — not in the provided material. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no direct occupant effect.
fha.fcDesc: Failure to annunciate a genuine failure condition — a real underlying failure produces no crew alert
fha.effCrew: A genuine failure condition occurs but is not annunciated; crew are unaware and take no action regarding it, so the effect is that of the unannunciated failure allowed to progress unmitigated.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot be grounded: severity equals that of the worst underlying failure whose annunciation fails, combined with the crew being unaware. The SDD does not enumerate the conditions alerted nor their aircraft effect, so the driving severity cannot be derived from the provided material. Left empty per abstention.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No direct effect on aircraft state; the alerting function that consolidates and prioritises every system's status into a single crew alert list with associated procedures is entirely lost, so subsequent failures are presented without consolidation, prioritisation or procedural guidance.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect confined to flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of consolidated crew alerting
fha.effCrew: Crew workload and error exposure increase substantially: they must detect, prioritise and diagnose any concurrent or subsequent failure without the consolidated prioritised alert list and associated procedures the flight deck is designed around.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Total loss of the aircraft's single consolidated crew-alerting function significantly reduces crew ability to cope with adverse operating conditions and could mask or delay response to a subsequent hazardous failure; proposed Hazardous per AC 25.1309-1B. CONFIRM: depends on independence and coverage of any residual annunciation the crew retains with consolidated alerting lost — not established in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect confined to flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Spurious fire or overheat warning with no fire present
fha.effCrew: Crew receives a fire/overheat warning with no fire present; the SDD does not state the assumed crew response (fire-handle actuation, engine shutdown) or its aircraft consequence, so the crew-effect chain cannot be fully grounded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD describes detection and the crew fire-handle action but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of acting on a spurious warning (e.g. precautionary shutdown of a serviceable engine or discharge of an extinguisher bottle). Effect on aircraft and the resulting severity are ungrounded — engineer to establish the assumed crew response before classifying.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: An actual fire or overheat in a monitored zone (engine nacelle, APU compartment, bleed duct runs, main gear bays, or hold) progresses undetected, so no warning is raised and no crew extinguishing action is initiated, allowing an uncontained fire to develop.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect confined to flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Failure to detect an actual fire or overheat condition
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no fire/overheat warning and takes no isolation or extinguishing action; first awareness may come only from secondary effects, by which point the fire may be unmanageable.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: Undetected fire in an engine nacelle or APU (fire zones) with no warning and no extinguishing action can lead to an uncontrolled fire and loss of the aircraft; proposed Catastrophic per AC 25.1309-1B. CONFIRM: worst-case zone and whether dual-loop AND logic (per §5.12.2) makes total detection failure the governing case for this aircraft-level condition. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: Fire/overheat detection is lost in a single monitored zone while detection is retained elsewhere; a fire originating in that one zone would progress undetected, but coverage of all other fire and overheat zones remains.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect confined to flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of detection in one monitored zone
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no warning for a fire or overheat originating in the affected zone; warning and extinguishing action remain available for all other zones.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without knowing which single zone is affected — the SDD monitors zones of very different consequence (engine nacelle/APU fire zones per §5.12.2 vs. main gear bay overheat), so the aircraft effect and severity depend on the worst applicable zone, which this condition does not name. Engineer to bound the governing zone.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: Overheat detection on the bleed duct runs and the main gear bays is lost while fire detection is retained; an overheat condition (e.g. a bleed duct leak or gear-bay overheat) would progress unannunciated up to the point it becomes a detectable fire.
fha.effPax: No occupants in the hold; effect confined to flight crew.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of overheat detection with fire detection retained
fha.effCrew: Crew receives no overheat warning and therefore no early cue to isolate a hot bleed duct or address a gear-bay overheat before it escalates; fire warning remains available.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify: the SDD states overheat detection is fitted to the bleed duct runs and main gear bays but does not state the aircraft-level consequence of an unannunciated overheat (e.g. duct burn-through, structural or systems damage) before it becomes a fire. Aircraft effect and severity are ungrounded pending that consequence analysis.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No detection of fire or overheat in any monitored zone (engine nacelles, APU, bleed ducts, gear bays, hold); a fire or overheat can develop and propagate undetected toward structure, fuel or systems.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of fire and overheat detection
fha.effCrew: Crew receive no fire/overheat warning and take no protective action; fire handles/extinguishing not commanded because the initiating condition is unknown.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Loss of detection across all fire zones means an engine/APU/bleed/gear fire progresses without crew awareness; effect on the aircraft depends on fire-propagation and structural/fuel-vulnerability judgement not in the SDD — confirm whether an undetected nacelle or wing-adjacent fire is Catastrophic. Detection is dual-loop per zone (AND logic), so simultaneous total loss is the concern; classification to be substantiated against fire-zone effects. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: One extinguisher bottle discharged into a nacelle with no fire; that agent charge is expended and unavailable for a subsequent genuine fire in that engine pair. Cross-plumbed second bottle remains for the pair.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Inadvertent extinguisher discharge with no fire present
fha.effCrew: Spurious discharge indication; crew assess and manage the affected engine; no immediate loss of control.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. Effect is reduced fire-extinguishing reserve for one engine pair, not loss of a flight function; the pair retains a second cross-plumbed bottle. Confirm against the dispatch/continued-flight case for a subsequent fire with one bottle expended. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: On a confirmed engine or APU fire the commanded discharge does not extinguish; fire continues and may propagate to structure, fuel or adjacent systems.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied; flight crew only exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Failure to extinguish on commanded discharge
fha.effCrew: Crew have detected and responded to the fire but the extinguishing means fails to arrest it; remaining options are engine shutdown, isolation and diversion.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED. An uncontrolled, detected engine/APU fire that cannot be extinguished depends on fire-propagation and structural/fuel-vulnerability effects not stated in the SDD — confirm whether a sustained nacelle fire adjacent to the wing/fuel is Hazardous or Catastrophic. Two bottles per pair mitigate a single-bottle failure, so this is failure of the extinguishing function itself. — engineer to confirm.

fha.fcDesc: Loss of automatic APU extinguishing
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — CANNOT CLASSIFY from the provided material. The SDD describes the APU bottle as a single dedicated bottle discharged AUTOMATICALLY on detection with the aircraft UNATTENDED; it does not state an in-flight aircraft-level effect of losing only the automatic path, nor whether a manual/crew discharge path for the APU exists in flight. Without the flight-phase applicability and the availability of an alternate discharge means, no effect can be stated and no severity derived. Needs engineering input: in-flight APU fire response and whether auto-discharge is the sole extinguishing path.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: With an engine or APU fire present, no means remains to extinguish or suppress it; fire may propagate within a nacelle or the APU compartment (fire zones per zonal model) with potential structural and adjacent-system damage.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of engine and APU fire extinguishing capability
fha.effCrew: Crew receive fire warning and actuate fire handles, but discharge is ineffective; crew must manage an uncontained fire condition and divert.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Hazardous: loss of the means to extinguish an engine/APU fire, coincident with a fire, threatens structure and adjacent systems and forces a diversion. Severity is coincident-with-fire; loss of extinguishing alone (no fire) is latent. §25.1309 objective for Hazardous is 1e-7/fh (engineer to confirm). Effect on aircraft depends on fire progression not quantified in the SDD. — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No aircraft handling effect directly; aircraft remains controllable.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no passenger oxygen fitted, no occupants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Complete loss of crew breathing oxygen supply
fha.effCrew: With no oxygen at any mask, a depressurisation, smoke or fume event leaves crew without breathing protection; incapacitation risk during descent/diversion. In the absence of such a triggering event the condition is latent until oxygen is demanded.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Hazardous: complete loss of crew oxygen removes the sole crew protection for a depressurisation/smoke/fume event during the descent and diversion the system is sized for; crew incapacitation is credible. Max operating altitude FL260 with low-differential hold bounds hypoxia time-of-useful-consciousness — engineer to confirm whether this supports Hazardous vs Catastrophic. §25.1309 Hazardous objective 1e-7/fh (to confirm). — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No direct aircraft handling effect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Reduced crew oxygen supply duration or reserve
fha.effCrew: Oxygen available but of shorter duration/reduced reserve; crew have breathing protection for a curtailed diversion time, constraining the time available to descend and divert.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Major: reserve/duration is degraded but protection remains for a triggering event; effect is a reduction in diversion margin rather than loss of protection. Whether the curtailed duration still covers the required diversion at FL260 is not quantified in the SDD — engineer to confirm; if the shortfall is severe this could rise to Hazardous. §25.1309 Major objective 1e-5/fh (to confirm). — engineer to confirm.

fha.effAc: No direct aircraft handling effect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Loss of oxygen to one or more mask stations
fha.effCrew: One or more of the four mask stations lose supply; affected crew member(s) lack breathing protection during a depressurisation/smoke/fume event while other stations remain supplied. With regulators independent per mask, remaining stations are unaffected.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). SEVERITY NOT DETERMINED by the model — Cannot classify without the operational assumption of how many stations are lost and whether a required crew member (nominal complement of two) retains protection. SDD states four mask stations and independent regulators but does not fix which/how many are affected; the aircraft-crew effect (and thus severity) turns on that. Engineer to specify the station-loss case.. Engineer to classify.

fha.effAc: No direct aircraft handling effect.
fha.effPax: Hold unoccupied in flight; no occupants exposed.
fha.fcDesc: Degraded oxygen delivery or contaminated supply at the mask
fha.effCrew: Crew don masks in a depressurisation/smoke/fume event but receive degraded or contaminated oxygen; protection is misleadingly present, risking hypoxia or exposure to contaminant without the crew recognising the shortfall. Malfunction (erroneous delivery) rather than loss.
fha.comments: AI-drafted (claude-opus-4-8). Severity rationale: PROPOSED Hazardous: a malfunction that delivers degraded/contaminated gas defeats the very protection the crew relies on during the triggering event and may be unrecognised (this is the Unaware M cell), so crew cannot compensate. Whether this reaches Catastrophic depends on the credible depressurisation exposure at FL260 — engineer to confirm. §25.1309 Hazardous objective 1e-7/fh (to confirm). — engineer to confirm.

assumptions.note: Agreed — SDD Appendix A explicitly leaves function derivation to the safety organisation.
assumptions.text: The aircraft-level functions listed are a valid derivation from the §5 system-purpose statements, since the SDD does not itself enumerate aircraft-level functions.
assumptions.ifWrong: The function names, groupings and one-level decomposition all change; downstream AFHA failure conditions trace to different functions.
assumptions.usedFor: Every add_function action in this turn.

citations.quote: It does not tell you what the aircraft-level functions are.

assumptions.rationale: Appendix A states the document deliberately omits the function list and leaves it to the safety organisation to derive.

assumptions.note: Matches §2.1 — resources supply other systems; structure carried by PRA/structural analysis.
assumptions.text: FUE, HYD, EPS and EWS are resources (not aircraft functions), and the nose-door load path and hold-floor hard points are structure, so all are excluded from functional decomposition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any of these must be captured as a behaviour, additional aircraft functions would be added and the FCIM/resource model changes.
assumptions.usedFor: Exclusion of FUE/HYD/EPS/EWS and nose-door/hard-point structure from the decomposition.

citations.quote: Four are treated as resources — they exist to supply other systems

assumptions.rationale: The SDD marks four systems as resources and identifies the door and hard points as structure, and the modeling rule bars authoring resources/structure as functions.

assumptions.text: Independence notes (e.g. single-engine loss, dual actuation, standby instrument segregation) reflect claimed architecture that must be tested, not confirmed independence.
assumptions.ifWrong: Independence notes on the affected sub-functions are removed or downgraded, altering later PSSA/CMA structure.
assumptions.usedFor: The Independence notes in the flight-controls, propulsion and avionics sub-functions.

citations.quote: a claim about independence that has to be tested rather than assumed

assumptions.rationale: The SDD explicitly flags several commonalities (A/B wing-root run, generator part-number commonality, identical ice detectors) as claims to be examined rather than established independence.

assumptions.text: SF-001 total loss is treated as complete loss of thrust generation, with asymmetric-thrust cases captured as partials.
assumptions.ifWrong: If asymmetry is not a distinct partial condition, the SF-001 partials[] array collapses to one entry.

citations.quote: Asymmetric thrust from an outboard engine at the 28 m moment arm is the sizing case for directional control

assumptions.rationale: The function list gives only the behaviour 'Produce propulsive thrust'; the SDD describes four engines but the FCIM must stay implementation-agnostic, so I abstracted engine count into thrust-generation capability.

assumptions.text: A combined failure condition — asymmetric thrust loss concurrent with degraded yaw control authority — is a distinct condition for the matrix Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the two are independent, no Combined-column entry is warranted and the engineer omits it.
assumptions.usedFor: Combined condition flag spanning SF-001 and SF-003

citations.quote: the resulting rudder authority requirement is carried in the flight-control sizing

assumptions.rationale: The SDD ties the outboard-engine-out case directly to rudder authority sizing, implying the two functions interact; the single-function FCIM cannot hold this, so it is flagged for the Combined column.

assumptions.text: The crew-unaware variants for SF-001/002/003/005 carry only slow/undetectable degradations, on the assumption fast losses annunciate via the alerting system.
assumptions.ifWrong: If fast losses can also go unannunciated, additional conditions migrate to the Unaware rows.

citations.quote: consolidates every system's status into a single prioritised crew alert list

assumptions.rationale: No effects or detection means exist yet in the model, so the Aware/Unaware split for most conditions cannot be fully grounded; I retained an Unaware row only for conditions that can develop below threshold.

assumptions.note: Rejected — asymmetry brakes only catch asymmetric cases. A slow SYMMETRIC high-lift drift annunciates nothing; adding an SF-004 Unaware row.
assumptions.text: SF-004 has no separate crew-unaware row because asymmetric high-lift is self-evident through aircraft response and the asymmetry brakes annunciate.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a slow symmetric high-lift drift can develop undetected, an SF-004 Unaware row is required.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-004 (single Aware row, no Unaware row)

citations.quote: through a common torque shaft with asymmetry brakes at each section

assumptions.rationale: Detection means are not yet modelled; the asymmetry-brake feature in the SDD suggests intrinsic detection, so I dismissed the unaware case per-condition rather than authoring an N/A row.

assumptions.text: The 'support' aspect of SF-006 is a structural-flotation property substantiated by structural analysis and PRA, not a functional failure condition, so it is excluded from the SF-006 malfunction cells.
assumptions.ifWrong: If support is intended as a functional behaviour here, SF-006 needs added total/partial conditions for loss of ground support/flotation.

citations.quote: The landing gear supports the aircraft on the ground, absorbs landing and taxi loads

assumptions.rationale: SF-006 bundles ground steering (a behaviour) with structural support; the modeling rule bars structural integrity from the functional FHA/FCIM.

assumptions.text: Nose-wheel steering can be commanded independently by tiller and by pedals, permitting a partial-loss condition where one command path is lost.
assumptions.ifWrong: The 'tiller lost / pedals retained' partial for SF-006 is invalid and should be removed.

citations.quote: commanded from tillers and rudder pedals, with a mechanical disconnect for towing

assumptions.rationale: The SDD states two command sources but does not confirm they are independently isolable; the partial condition depends on it.

assumptions.text: An erroneous 'locked' indication while the door is not fully locked can persist undetected because both sensing paths report status but need not agree to show locked in every failure mode.
assumptions.ifWrong: If disagreement is annunciated, the SF-007 unaware row collapses into the Aware row and the crew-unaware malfunction is removed.

citations.quote: Lock engagement is sensed by two dissimilar and independently routed circuits

assumptions.rationale: Dual dissimilar sensing is described but the voting/disagreement logic is not given, forcing this assumption for the SF-007 unaware malfunction.

assumptions.text: A single-station restraint loss can develop below the annunciation threshold because in-flight indication exists but its detection threshold and latency are unspecified.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any tension loss is promptly annunciated, the SF-008 unaware partial is invalid and removed.

citations.quote: Loss of tension on any strap is annunciated in flight

assumptions.rationale: The SDD confirms annunciation of tension loss but gives no threshold, so an undetected single-station partial cannot be excluded.

assumptions.text: The single instrumented tension loop is a common monitoring path such that its failure can leave an actual restraint loss unannunciated with no crew cue.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a redundant or cross-check cue exists, the SF-009 unaware failure-to-annunciate is not credible and should move to Aware.

citations.quote: The restraint tension monitoring loop is a single instrumented loop and its coverage is a recorded item

assumptions.rationale: The loop is stated to be single; a monitor failure defeating annunciation is the basis for the SF-009 crew-unaware condition.

assumptions.text: A slow pressure-differential drift can develop below crew detection despite continuous cabin-altitude display, because slow rates may not trip an alert.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a rate/threshold alert covers slow drift, the SF-010 unaware row is removed and the drift becomes an Aware malfunction.

citations.quote: Positive and negative pressure relief valves protect the structure independently of the control system

assumptions.rationale: Differential/cabin altitude is displayed but alert thresholds and rate-of-change logic are not specified, forcing this assumption for the SF-010 unaware malfunction.

assumptions.text: SF-011 conditioning tolerates a degraded schedule, so its partial-loss cell splits into within-schedule and outside-schedule degradation.
assumptions.ifWrong: If no acceptable degraded conditioning schedule exists, the two partials collapse to a single partial-loss condition.

citations.quote: Single-pack operation is permitted with a reduced hold conditioning schedule

assumptions.rationale: The FCIM within/outside-limits partial split needs a stated acceptable degraded mode; the SDD gives single-pack reduced schedule but not the limit values.

assumptions.text: Ice protection and probe protection failures can develop below crew detection thresholds, justifying a crew-Unaware row for each.
assumptions.ifWrong: If every ice/probe-protection loss is annunciated, the Unaware rows for SF-012 and SF-013 are removed.
assumptions.usedFor: SF-012 Unaware row, SF-013 Unaware row

citations.quote: Electrical zones are independently supplied and a lost zone is annunciated

assumptions.rationale: Awareness split needs a stated alert per condition; the SDD annunciates lost electrical zones but does not confirm coverage of every accretion or probe-loss case.

assumptions.text: Misleading information consistent across the primary display chain can defeat crew cross-check, justifying an SF-014 crew-Unaware misleading-information condition.
assumptions.ifWrong: If the standby instrument always exposes primary-source errors, the consistent-misleading-information Unaware condition drops.

citations.quote: an independent standby instrument that shares no supply, no sensor and no processing with the primary displays

assumptions.rationale: The Unaware misleading-data condition depends on whether the independent standby instrument reliably reveals a common-source error; the SDD states independence but not detection coverage.

assumptions.text: Failure to annunciate a genuine failure (silent alerting loss) is undetectable to the crew, justifying an SF-015 crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If a health monitor annunciates loss of alerting integrity, the SF-015 Unaware conditions move to the Aware row.

citations.quote: driven by two independent processing channels

assumptions.rationale: A suppressed-alert condition is by nature crew-unaware; the SDD does not describe a monitor that would reveal loss of the alerting function itself.

assumptions.text: SF-017 covers engine and APU fire extinguishing only; hold smoke suppression is deliberately not fitted and is not an SF-017 capability.
assumptions.ifWrong: If hold suppression is later fitted, SF-017 gains a hold-suppression loss condition and the FHA/PRA substantiation item changes.

citations.quote: The hold has smoke detection at nine stations along its length and no suppression

assumptions.rationale: The function name and SDD scope engine/APU extinguishing; the hold has detection but no suppression, so a hold-suppression loss condition cannot be authored against SF-017.

assumptions.text: Failure of SF-016 to detect an actual fire can develop below crew detection thresholds and therefore keeps its own crew-Unaware row.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any loss of detection is always annunciated, the crew-Unaware SF-016 row collapses into the Aware row.

citations.quote: degrading to single-loop logic on loss of one loop

assumptions.rationale: The dual-loop AND-then-single-loop degradation means a detection gap need not annunciate, so the undetected-failure-to-detect variant is not evident to the crew.

assumptions.text: Loss of fire detection concurrent with an actual fire is a candidate COMBINED failure condition for SF-016 to be filed in the matrix Combined column.
assumptions.ifWrong: If not a genuine combined case, the Combined-column entry is dropped; individual rows are unaffected.

citations.quote: detects fire and overheat in the zones where they must be detected

assumptions.rationale: ARP4761A Table A3 permits combined conditions across related sub-functions; the detect-and-extinguish pairing is a plausible combined case the function list alone flags but does not classify.

assumptions.text: Crew indication and mitigation detail for these conditions cannot be grounded until AFHA effects and detection means exist, so those fields are left empty.
assumptions.ifWrong: If detection/indication means are already fixed, the empty indication/mitigation fields would be populated.
assumptions.usedFor: indication and mitigation fields on all SF-016/017/018 rows
assumptions.rationale: The FCIM feeds the AFHA; indication/mitigation columns depend on effects and detection means that the FHA has not yet produced.

assumptions.text: For every SF-001 condition the flight crew (nominal two) are the only occupants at risk in flight because the hold is unoccupied.
assumptions.ifWrong: If any occupant can be in the hold in flight, the occupant-effect column and potentially the severity of every SF-001 row would need to escalate for occupant harm.
assumptions.usedFor: effPax on SF-001-M, SF-001-M2, SF-001-M3, SF-001-PL, SF-001-PL2

citations.quote: The hold is not occupied in flight. The aircraft carries flight crew only
